claims.text: Using configurational entropy in high-entropy-alloy design can stabilize a single-phase solid solution.
Configurational entropy produces entropy-driven thermodynamic stabilization.
Kinetic stabilization prevents phase separation in multicomponent alloys.
Sluggish diffusion prevents elemental segregation in multicomponent alloys.
Entropy-driven and kinetic stabilization enable uniform alloy structures to form from traditionally immiscible elements.
The intervention improves determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention improves determination of fusion enthalpy relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention improves determination of fusion entropy relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention improves determination of the volume change at the solid-to-fluid transition relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The intervention improves determination of dense-fluid heat capacity relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
The proposed stabilization mechanism remains applicable to both solid and fluid states around the high-temperature transition.
There are insufficient data on how configurational entropy affects the relevant thermodynamic properties of high-entropy materials.
Current computational models have limitations for determining these thermodynamic properties.
Current experimental methods have limitations for determining these thermodynamic properties.
